column2: 古英语 scield ← 原始西日耳曼语 *skeldu ← 原始日耳曼语 *skelduz ← 原始印欧语 *(s)kelH-（切、劈）
column3: a broad piece of armour held to block blows
column5: He raised his shield against the arrows.|Trees shield the garden from wind.
column6: a broad plate held up to take the blow – 举起来承接打击的一块宽板
column7: 盾牌：手持挡击的防具|保护：挡在前面使不受害

column2: 古英语 sċiftan（分开、安排）← 原始西日耳曼语 *skiftijan ← 原始日耳曼语 *skiftijaną
column3: a change of position, or a work period
column5: There was a slow shift in opinion.|She works the night shift.
column6: moving something over to another place or slot – 把东西挪到另一位置或另一段
column7: 转移：位置或重心挪动|班次：轮流上工的一段时间

column2: 古英语 sċilling ← 原始西日耳曼语 *skilling ← 原始日耳曼语 *skillingaz
column3: a former British coin worth twelve old pence
column5: The book cost only a few shillings.|He kept an old shilling for luck.
column6: the old coin worth a twentieth of a pound – 旧制中值一镑二十分之一的硬币

column2: 古英语 sċīnan ← 原始西日耳曼语 *skīnan ← 原始日耳曼语 *skīnaną
column3: to give out or reflect bright light
column5: The sun shone all afternoon.|He shined his boots before leaving.
column6: giving off or throwing back light – 发出或反回光
column7: 发光：自身放出光|照耀：光照到某处使之明亮

column2: 古英语 sċip ← 原始西日耳曼语 *skip ← 原始日耳曼语 *skipą（船、槽）
column3: a large boat for carrying people or goods by sea
column5: The ship left port at dawn.|They ship goods to twelve countries.
column6: a large vessel that crosses water – 渡水而行的大型舟具
column7: 船：航行于水上的大型舟具|运送：用船或其它方式发运

column2: 由 ship ＋ -ment 构成
column3: a load of goods sent together
column5: The shipment arrived three days late.|They packed the shipment overnight.
column6: a batch sent off as one consignment – 作为一批发出去的货
column7: 货运：整批发出的货物|装运：把货装上并发出

column2: 古英语 sċyrte（短衣）← 原始西日耳曼语 *skurtijā ← 原始日耳曼语 *skurtaz（短）← 原始印欧语 *(s)ker-（切断）；与 skirt 同源
column3: a garment for the upper body with a collar and sleeves
column5: He ironed a white shirt for the interview.|Her shirt had short sleeves.
column6: the short upper garment cut to the body – 依身裁短的上装

column2: 中古荷兰语 schokken（推、震）或中古法语 choquer（碰撞）← 古荷兰语 *skokkan ← 原始日耳曼语 *skukkaną（摇动）
column3: a sudden upsetting event, or a violent impact
column5: The news came as a real shock.|The blast shocked windows across town.
column6: a sudden jolt that unsettles – 猛然一撞使人或物失稳
column7: 震惊：突发之事使人心神大动|冲击：猛烈撞击或影响

column2: 古英语 sċōh ← 原始西日耳曼语 *skōh ← 原始日耳曼语 *skōhaz，更早词源未定
column3: an outer covering for the foot
column5: He tied his left shoe again.|These shoes pinch my toes.
column6: the firm covering worn on the foot – 穿在脚上的硬质外覆

column2: 古英语 scēotan ← 原始西日耳曼语 *skeutan ← 原始日耳曼语 *skeutaną ← 原始印欧语 *(s)kewd-（射、抛）
column3: to fire a weapon or send something out fast
column5: He shot twice and missed both times.|Rockets shoot upward at great speed.
column6: sending something out fast and straight – 使某物又快又直地射出去
column7: 射击：用武器发射弹丸|发射：把物体高速送出

column2: 古英语 sċoppa（棚、摊）← 原始日耳曼语 *skupp-（仓、棚）
column3: a place where goods are sold, or to buy goods
column5: The shop opens at nine each morning.|We shop for food on Saturdays.
column6: a booth set up to sell from – 搭起来卖东西的摊铺
column7: 商店：出售商品的场所|购物：去买东西这件事

column2: 由 shop ＋ keeper 复合而成
column3: a person who owns or manages a small shop
column5: The shopkeeper knew every regular customer.|A shopkeeper locked up at six.
column6: the one who keeps the shop – 看守并经营店铺的人

column2: 中古英语 schore ← 古英语 *sċora ← 原始日耳曼语 *skurô（崖、多石的岸）
column3: the land along the edge of a sea or lake
column5: They walked along the rocky shore.|The boat reached shore before dark.
column6: the land where water stops – 水止于此的那条陆边
column7: 海岸：海与陆相接的一带|岸边：水体边缘的陆地

column2: 古英语 sċeort ← 原始西日耳曼语 *skurt ← 原始日耳曼语 *skurtaz ← 原始印欧语 *(s)ker-（切）；与 shirt、skirt 同源
column3: measuring little from end to end, or lasting little time
column5: He gave a short answer.|The film is quite short.
column6: cut off before reaching far – 还没伸远就被截住
column7: 短的：长度或时段小|矮的：高度不大

column2: 由 short ＋ -age 构成
column3: a situation in which there is not enough of something
column5: A water shortage hit the region.|There is no shortage of ideas.
column6: the state of falling short of what is needed – 距所需还差一截的状态
column7: 短缺：供应少于需要|不足：数量或程度未达要求

column2: 由 short ＋ coming 复合而成
column3: a fault that makes something less than adequate
column5: The plan has one serious shortcoming.|He admitted his own shortcomings.
column6: where something comes up short – 某处没够上标准
column7: 缺点：不足之处|短处：相对薄弱的方面

column2: 由 short ＋ hand（书写笔迹）复合而成
column3: a quick way of writing using symbols
column5: She took the minutes in shorthand.|Shorthand saved reporters much time.
column6: a shortened hand for writing fast – 为快写而缩省的笔法

column2: 古英语 sċortlīċe，由 short ＋ -ly 构成
column3: in a short time from now
column5: The train will arrive shortly.|She left shortly after the call.
column6: after only a short interval – 只隔很短一段之后
column7: 很快：不需多久就会发生|随即：紧跟着就

column2: 古英语 sċeot ← 原始日耳曼语 *skutą，与 shoot 同支
column3: the firing of a gun, or an attempt
column5: A single shot broke the silence.|He had one shot at the title.
column6: one discharge sent out – 射出去的那一发
column7: 射击：开枪这个动作|一枪：单次发射或单次尝试

column2: 古英语 sċuldor ← 原始西日耳曼语 *skuldru，更早词源未定
column3: the joint where the arm meets the body
column5: She tapped him on the shoulder.|He carried the sack on one shoulder.
column6: where the arm joins the trunk – 手臂与躯干相接之处
column7: 肩：上臂与躯干连接的部位|肩部：该部位所在的一带

column2: 中古英语 shouten，更早词源不明；或与 shoot 有关，或出古诺尔斯语 skúta（讥斥）
column3: to say something very loudly
column5: He shouted across the crowded room.|A shout came from the yard.
column6: sending the voice out with force – 用力把声音送出去
column7: 呼喊：放开嗓子叫|大叫：高声叫出

column2: 古英语 sċūfan ← 原始西日耳曼语 *skeuban ← 原始日耳曼语 *skeubaną
column3: to push someone or something roughly
column5: He shoved the door with his shoulder.|Someone shoved me from behind.
column6: pushing with sudden force – 突然使力往前顶
column7: 推搡：粗暴地推来推去|挤：用身体挤开

column2: 古英语 scēawian（看、展示）← 原始西日耳曼语 *skauwōn ← 原始日耳曼语 *skawwōną（看）
column3: to let something be seen, or a public performance
column5: She showed us the old photographs.|The show runs until December.
column6: putting something where it can be seen – 把东西放到可被看见的位置
column7: 展示：使人看到|演出：面向观众的表演

column2: 古英语 sċūr ← 原始西日耳曼语 *skūru ← 原始日耳曼语 *skūrō（骤雨）
column3: a short fall of rain, or a wash under falling water
column5: A shower passed over the valley.|He takes a shower before work.
column6: water coming down in a brief burst – 短时间落下的一阵水
column7: 淋浴：站在落水下冲洗|阵雨：下一阵就停的雨

column2: 中古英语 schrewed（邪恶的），出 schrewe（恶人）← 古英语 sċrēawa；16 世纪起转为「机敏」义，17 世纪渐成褒义
column3: able to judge people and situations quickly and well
column5: She made a shrewd guess about it.|He is a shrewd negotiator.
column6: quick to see through to what matters – 一眼看穿要害
column7: 精明的：判断快而准|老练的：因历练而不易被蒙

column2: 古英语 sċrincan ← 原始日耳曼语 *skrinkwaną
column3: to become smaller in size or amount
column5: Wool shrinks in very hot water.|The market shrank by a fifth.
column6: drawing in so as to take less room – 往里收使占的地方变少
column7: 收缩：体积或长度变小|缩小：数量或规模减少

column2: 中古英语 schruggen，或出北日耳曼语支，与丹麦语 skrugge（弯身）同类
column3: to raise the shoulders to show doubt or indifference
column5: She shrugged and walked away.|He gave a small shrug.
column6: lifting the shoulders instead of answering – 抬肩代替作答

column2: 古英语 sċyttan（拉上门闩）← 原始西日耳曼语 *skuttjan ← 原始日耳曼语 *skutjaną
column3: to move something into a closed position
column5: Please shut the gate behind you.|The shop shuts at seven.
column6: bringing a bolt or leaf across an opening – 把闩或扇挪过来堵住口
column7: 关闭：使不再开着|合上：把两面并到一起

column2: 由 shut ＋ -er 构成
column3: a hinged cover for a window, or the part of a camera that opens
column5: They closed the shutters before the storm.|The camera shutter clicked just once.
column6: the cover that shuts an opening – 把开口关上的那块盖
column7: 百叶窗：窗外可开合的板|快门：相机上控制曝光的开合件

column2: 古英语 sċytel（梭、箭）与 sċyttel（门闩）两支合流 ← 原始日耳曼语 *skutilaz；1338 年起指织机上的梭，取其在经线间「被射过去」之意
column3: a vehicle running back and forth over a short route
column5: A shuttle runs between the two terminals.|The weaver threw the shuttle across.
column6: something shot back and forth along a fixed path – 沿固定路线来回被送过去的东西
column7: 穿梭班车：两点间往复的车|梭子：织机上牵纬线来回穿的器件
